general_causes: Back pain is common and can be linked in general terms to muscle strain, poor posture, long sitting, lifting, or sleeping awkwardly.
Most short-term back pain improves gradually with movement and time.
see_doctor_if: Pain follows an injury, or comes with numbness, weakness, or loss of bladder or bowel control.
Pain is severe, lasts more than a few weeks, or comes with fever or unexplained weight loss.
Pain does not improve with gentle movement and rest.
what_usually_helps: Stay gently active rather than staying in bed all day, unless a clinician advises otherwise.
Change position regularly, take short walks, and use a warm compress if that helps.
Check your chair, desk, and lifting technique for obvious strain.

general_causes: A blocked nose often comes with a cold, flu, allergies, or dry air.
It can make sleeping and breathing through the nose harder for a few days.
see_doctor_if: Blockage lasts more than 10 days, affects only one side, or comes with severe facial pain or fever.
There is bloody discharge, or breathing becomes difficult.
Blockage keeps coming back at the same time of year and may be linked to allergies.
what_usually_helps: Use saline nasal spray or rinse if that helps, following the product instructions.
Breathe in steam from a warm shower, and keep the bedroom air comfortable.
Sleep with your head slightly raised if that helps you breathe.

general_causes: Colds are usually caused by common viruses and spread through coughs, sneezes, and close contact.
Symptoms often include a runny or blocked nose, sore throat, sneezing, and mild tiredness.
see_doctor_if: Symptoms last more than 10 days or get worse after first improving.
You have a high fever, severe headache, chest pain, or difficulty breathing.
You have a weakened immune system or a long-term lung condition and symptoms worsen.
what_usually_helps: Rest and drink fluids as appropriate.
Use saline nasal spray or rinse if that helps you breathe more comfortably, following the product instructions.
Keep the air comfortable and avoid smoke and strong smells where possible.

general_causes: Headaches are common and can be linked in general terms to stress, poor sleep, dehydration, eye strain, missed meals, caffeine changes, or illness such as a cold.
This list is general information only. It does not explain the cause of any one person's headache.
see_doctor_if: The headache is severe, sudden, or the worst you have ever had.
It follows a head injury, or comes with fever and a stiff neck, confusion, slurred speech, weakness, or vision loss.
It keeps coming back, lasts more than a few days, or interferes with work, sleep, or daily life.
It is a new severe headache in pregnancy.
what_usually_helps: Rest in a quiet, dark room if possible.
Drink fluids as appropriate and eat normally if you have missed a meal.
Take regular breaks from screens and bright light.
Note when the headache started, how severe it is, and what you tried, so you can share that with a clinician if needed.

general_causes: A sore throat often comes with a cold or flu, and can also be caused by dry air, shouting, or smoke.
Most sore throats improve on their own within a few days.
see_doctor_if: The sore throat is severe, lasts more than a week, or keeps coming back.
You have difficulty swallowing or breathing, a high fever, or swollen glands that do not improve.
You notice blood in saliva or a rash with the sore throat.
what_usually_helps: Drink warm fluids such as tea with honey, if honey is suitable for you.
Gargle with warm salt water, if that helps.
Rest your voice and avoid smoke where possible.

general_causes: Stomach upset can be linked in general terms to eating too much or too quickly, rich or spicy food, stress, travel, or a stomach bug.
This is general information only and does not explain any one person's symptoms.
see_doctor_if: You cannot keep fluids down, or you show signs of dehydration such as very little urine, dizziness, or confusion.
There is blood in vomit or stool, severe abdominal pain, or a high fever.
Symptoms last more than a few days or keep coming back.
what_usually_helps: Eat small, plain meals if you feel able to eat, and drink fluids little and often.
Rest and avoid alcohol and very rich or spicy food until you feel better.
Note what you ate, any medicines you took, and whether symptoms change.

general_causes: Tiredness can be linked in general terms to poor sleep, stress, low activity, illness, or changes in routine.
This is general information only and does not explain any one person's tiredness.
see_doctor_if: Tiredness lasts more than a few weeks, is severe, or comes with other symptoms such as weight change, breathlessness, or low mood.
It interferes with work, study, or daily life.
You have a long-term condition and tiredness suddenly worsens.
what_usually_helps: Keep a regular sleep routine and a dark, quiet bedroom where possible.
Take short daylight walks and regular breaks from screens.
Eat regularly and drink fluids as appropriate, and note sleep and activity in the diary.
